sections.h2: How does selling a house in Georgetown, KY work?
sections.html:
Georgetown owners weigh an agent listing, a sale handled alone and a cash purchase, and Scott County's offices handle the tax bill, the recorded deed and, for owners who fell behind, the delinquent-tax process. The city is the Scott County seat and the sixth-largest in Kentucky, counted at 37,086 in 2020, with the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate at 40,883.

It is also the highest-priced of the four cities in this group, with the largest households and the highest income, which sets the tone for the local market.

Georgetown has the largest share of homeowners, the largest households and the youngest population of the four cities, with 25.6% under 18 and only 10.9% over 65. About 69.4% of residents 16 and over are in the labor force, also the highest of the group.

The 2020 count found 13,979 households in 14,800 housing units, 5.5% of them vacant, with a rental vacancy rate of 7.1% and a median age of 33.1. Households with children under 18 made up 38.3% of the total, and 48.9% were married couples. Georgetown College plays football at Toyota Stadium, which also hosted the Lexington SC professional soccer club before it moved to Lexington.

sections.h2: Where is Georgetown and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Georgetown sits in the Bluegrass, north of Lexington. Interstate 75 passes east of downtown with exits 125, 126, 127 and 129, putting downtown Lexington 16 miles south and Cincinnati 69 miles north. U.S. 25 runs through the center, U.S. 62 forms a bypass along the south and east, and U.S. 460 leads 18 miles west to Frankfort.

Baptist minister Elijah Craig brought a congregation here in 1782 and founded a settlement called Lebanon, incorporated in 1784 around the Royal Spring. The name changed to George Town for George Washington in 1790, Scott County was formed in 1792, and the spelling became Georgetown in 1846. After the Civil War the town became a rail hub, and the line from Frankfort carried much of the region's bourbon toward the Ohio River.

The modern city dates from Toyota's decision in 1985 to build a plant here. The plant, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky, opened in 1988 and assembles the Camry, Lexus ES and RAV4. In the city's 2018 annual financial report, Toyota led employers with 10,019 people, followed by Scott County Schools at 1,219 and Adient at 743. The population climbed from 18,080 in 2000 to 29,098 in 2010 and 37,086 in 2020.

Highs average about 86 degrees in July, lows reach about 25 in January, and precipitation totals roughly 45 inches a year. Before a showing, check gutters, roof drainage and basement moisture.

sections.h2: Which schools and neighborhoods serve Georgetown homes?
sections.html:
Scott County Schools operates the public schools: nine elementaries, three middle schools, and two high schools, Scott County High and Great Crossing High, the latter opened in 2019. Elkhorn Crossing School gives some sophomores and juniors a program that blends academics with career training.

  • Georgetown College, a private liberal arts college, is downtown, and the Baptist Seminary of Kentucky is also in the city.
  • The Oxford Historic District downtown, and Greek Revival Ward Hall just outside the city, carry National Register listings.
  • Private options include St. John, Providence Christian Academy and Keystone Montessori.

sections.h2: How does Scott County collect property tax and what happens if bills go unpaid?
sections.html:
The Scott County Sheriff collects tax for 28 districts, and bills are normally mailed on November 1. The sheriff does not set values: questions about assessment go to the Scott County PVA, on the second floor of the courthouse at 101 East Main Street, or by phone at (502) 863-7885.

The county clerk's published timeline for bills left unpaid is a useful warning for anyone behind on taxes before a sale:

  • April 15: delinquent certificates move to the County Clerk's office.
  • May and June: the County Attorney mails two notices, and the first offers a payment agreement to eligible owners.
  • June 30: last day to enter a payment agreement.
  • July 1: advertising costs are added to bills still unpaid, which are published in the newspaper.
  • Late summer: payment is due by a cutoff before the annual delinquent tax sale.

Payment can be cash, cashier's check, money order or card, and cards add a 2.75% vendor fee. When a bill transfers, a 10% penalty and the sheriff's add-on fee are already attached, and interest runs at 1% per month. An owner with delinquent tax should get the clerk's payoff figure before choosing a closing date.

sections.h2: What does a Georgetown seller pay in transfer tax and where is the deed recorded?
sections.html:
The seller owes $0.50 for each $500 of deed value, rounded up per block. At the Census median of $265,400 that is $265.50 (531 blocks). The Scott County Clerk, at 101 East Main Street, collects it as the deed is filed, and the office keeps weekday hours from 8:30 to 4:30 at (502) 863-7875.

Owners past 65 or with a total disability may qualify for the state homestead exemption, $49,100 in the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, through the Scott County PVA. It attaches to the person, so a buyer files a new application.

sections.h2: Who handles permits and zoning questions in Georgetown?
sections.html:
The City of Georgetown handles building permits for both the city and Scott County, from the Building Inspection Department at 125 West Clinton Street. Zoning, plats and floodplain information come from the Georgetown-Scott County Planning Commission, which offers a zoning map and a plat finder on its site and answers at (502) 867-3701.

For a house with an addition or a finished basement, ask the building department whether the permits were closed. A buyer's title review is simpler when the paperwork matches the house. If the house has been rented by the night, ask the planning office whether a registration applies.

sections.h2: Which route works for a Georgetown house?
sections.html:
Before you compare offers, gather these items:

  • The current and prior year tax bills from the sheriff, plus any delinquent certificate from the clerk.
  • A mortgage payoff statement, and the release for any other recorded lien.
  • Permit records from the City of Georgetown for additions or major repairs.
  • Leases and tenant contacts for any rented unit.

A house in good order with time to market suits an agent. A private sale needs an attorney for the contract and deed. Deferred repairs, tenants, delinquent taxes or an estate point toward a cash offer. Whatever the route, judge offers by what remains after payoff, deed tax, prorated property tax and repair credits.

faqs.q: How much deed tax applies to a Georgetown sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays $0.50 per $500 block. For a house at the $265,400 Census median that is $265.50, taken by the Scott County Clerk when the deed is filed.

faqs.q: When does Scott County mail property tax bills?
faqs.a: The Scott County Sheriff normally mails them on November 1. The bill lists the due dates, how to avoid penalties and what to do if a mortgage company pays.

faqs.q: What happens to unpaid Georgetown property taxes?
faqs.a: Around April 15 they move to the Scott County Clerk. The County Attorney mails notices in May and June, advertising costs attach on July 1, and a bill still open can go to the annual delinquent tax sale.

faqs.q: Which office answers questions on a Georgetown assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Scott County Property Valuation Administrator at (502) 863-7885. The sheriff only collects what the PVA assessed.

faqs.q: Where do I get a building permit in Georgetown?
faqs.a: The City of Georgetown's Building Inspection Department, 125 West Clinton Street, issues permits for both Georgetown and Scott County. Zoning and plat questions go to the Georgetown-Scott County Planning Commission, (502) 867-3701.
